official.deadline_note: A single global application deadline is stated identically on the official application page and in the 2027 instructions; no separate institutional deadline is published.
official.application_cycle: 2027 Fellowship cycle (application opened 22 September 2026; institutes run mid-June through early August 2027)
official.status_note: The official application page lists the 2027 cycle timeline: application opened 22 September 2026, deadline 13 October 2026, semi-finalist interviews November 2026 to January 2027, notifications February/March 2027, visa processing and pre-departure orientations March to May 2027, and the Fellowship beginning in the United States in June 2027. As of the verification date the window was open but about to close.
official.tuition_coverage_note: This is a non-degree programme, so no tuition is charged and no degree is awarded. The official 2027 instructions state that if selected, 'the U.S. Government will cover all program costs,' listing 'A six-week institute' among the funded costs.
benefits: There is no fee to apply for the Mandela Washington Fellowship.
If you are selected for the Fellowship, the U.S. Government will cover all program costs.

Round-trip travel from Fellow's home city to the United States and domestic U.S. travel as required by the program; Fellows must depart from their country of residence within an eligible Fellowship country in Africa.
A six-week institute at a U.S. college or university, together with housing and meals during the program.
A limited accident and sickness benefit plan; an optional four-week Professional Development Experience (for up to 50 Fellows) will include support for housing, meals, and transportation.
eligibility: Are between the ages of 25 and 35 as of the application deadline (October 13, 2026), although exceptional applicants ages 21-24 may be considered.

Are citizens of one of 49 listed Sub-Saharan African countries and are residents of one of those countries, permanently residing there as of February 1, 2027, and at the beginning of the Fellowship in June 2027.
Are not U.S. citizens or permanent residents of the United States, and are eligible to receive a United States J-1 visa.
Are not employees or immediate family members (spouses, parents, children, or siblings) of employees of the U.S. Government, including a U.S. embassy or consulate.
Are proficient in reading, writing, and speaking English.
Are not alumni or prior participants of the Mandela Washington Fellowship.
requirements: Applications must be submitted using the online application system at apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org; applications and information submitted via email or other means will not be considered, and only one application per applicant is permitted.

All application questions must be answered in English, and answers must be your own original work; applications that copy language from other Fellowship applications or other sources will be disqualified as plagiarism, and any use of technology (including AI) must be disclosed in the application.
All fields marked with a red asterisk must be completed, and every required section must be marked 'Completed' before clicking 'Submit Application' on the application dashboard.
All submitted applications are final: once submitted, no additional information can be added and no changes can be made.

If selected as a semi-finalist, you must provide a copy of your international passport (if available) or other government-issued photo identification at the interview, and documentation verifying age, citizenship, and residency; discrepancies or false information render the application invalid and the applicant ineligible.
documents: Full legal name, date of birth, and biological sex exactly as they appear on your passport and/or official government-issued identification.

Passport status (country of issue and expiration date): you do not need a passport to apply, but selected finalists must have a passport valid through at least February 28, 2028, or March 31, 2028 if selected for the Professional Development Experience.

Resume/CV entered in the online system within the published entry limits (up to five positions, five educational institutions, five trainings/certifications, five community and volunteer roles, up to 10 awards, eight languages, 10 computer or software skills, publications and affiliations).
English language self-assessment: whether English is your native language plus a proficiency level for each skill.
Personal statements (four required essays plus a 200-word track-fit essay), Leadership Assessment responses, and your ranked preference of the three institute tracks.
Optional Professional Development Experience application with three additional essays, and a Technology Use Disclosure listing the technology used to prepare the application.
selection_criteria: Proficiency speaking, reading, and writing in English.
A proven record of accomplishment in business, trade, emerging technologies, governance, and/or security.
A demonstrated and clear interest in building and maintaining partnerships with American organizations and businesses that advance shared goals.
A commitment to return to Sub-Saharan Africa and contribute skills and talents to build and serve their communities.
The ability to work cooperatively in groups and to respect others.
Demonstrated adaptability and the ability to lead effectively in varying and changing environments.
coverage: Round-trip travel from Fellow's home city to the United States and domestic U.S. travel as required by the program.
A six-week institute (no degree is awarded).
Housing and meals during the program.
A limited accident and sickness benefit plan.

Not funded: the U.S. Department of State, IREX, institutes, and/or PDE Hosts will not provide funds to cover Fellows' salaries while away from work or funds for personal purchases, such as support for Fellows' home organizations or gifts for family.
application_method: Create a separate account at apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org; signing up for YALI Network updates does not create an application account. The system is mobile-friendly, functions in low-bandwidth environments, and saves progress.

Complete the Eligibility section in full to proceed, then General Information and Resume/CV (recommended first, since its entries auto-populate later sections), Demographic Information, Contact, Current Professional and/or Educational Experience, YALI Engagement, Previous U.S. Experience, and English Language sections.

Complete Institute Track and Sector Alignment (ranking the three tracks and the 200-word track-fit essay), the Leadership Assessment, and the Personal Statements (four essays), plus the optional PDE essays if applying.
Complete the Technology Use Disclosure, confirm all required sections show 'Completed,' then click 'Submit Application' on the dashboard before 16:00/4:00 PM GMT on Tuesday, October 13, 2026.
official.application_route: Apply online only through the online application system at apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org; paper or email applications are not accepted.
official.study_mode: Full-time: an intensive six-week programme in which Fellows are expected to be fully engaged, with full attendance at and participation in all required activities, events, and sessions.
official.citizenship_residency: Must be a citizen of one of the 49 listed Sub-Saharan African countries and permanently resident there as of February 1, 2027, and at the beginning of the Fellowship in June 2027; U.S. citizens and permanent residents are not eligible, and residents of the United States or of any non-eligible country are not eligible under any circumstances.
official.international_eligibility: Open only to citizens and residents of the 49 listed Sub-Saharan African countries; residents of the United States or of any other non-eligible country are not eligible under any circumstances.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field-of-study or professional-sector restriction; applicants rank three institute tracks in order of preference: Business and Trade, Emerging Technologies, or Governance and Security. Applications from members of the military, defense ministries, police, and other law enforcement are eligible.
official.duration: A six-week institute at a U.S. college or university, from mid-June through early August 2027, plus an optional four-week Professional Development Experience; selected PDE Fellows must be in the United States for approximately 10 weeks in total.
official.description: The Mandela Washington Fellowship for Young African Leaders is the exchange component of the U.S. Government's Young African Leaders Initiative (YALI), a program of the U.S. Department of State with funding provided by the U.S. Government and administered by IREX. It brings up to 550 accomplished young African leaders to the United States for a comprehensive executive-style program: a six-week institute at a U.S. college or university combining academic coursework, professional site visits, structured networking, community service, and cultural activities in one of three tracks (Business and Trade, Emerging Technologies, or Governance and Security), plus an optional four-week Professional Development Experience for up to 50 Fellows and ongoing alumni opportunities.
official.region: North America (United States); applicants from Sub-Saharan Africa
official.program_type: Non-degree executive-style exchange programme of the U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs, administered by IREX; no degree is awarded.
official.english_requirement: High-level proficiency in written and spoken English is required, because all activities (academic sessions, discussions, meetings, cultural activities, and social interactions) will be in English; proficiency is assessed through the online application self-assessment (Absolute Beginner to Very Advanced) and, for semi-finalists, the embassy interview, and TOEFL scores are not required. All application components must be written in English; applicants who are deaf should indicate proficiency in reading and writing standard English and in American Sign Language, since interpretation in the United States may only be available in ASL.

verification.notes: Official application page, application FAQs, About page, and the 2027 Application Instructions PDF (downloaded from the awarding body's own domain) were read directly; no monetary award figure is published because funding is provided as in-kind coverage of all program costs, so amount/currency/period are recorded as unconfirmed.

applicant_utility.summary: With roughly 550 places drawn from 49 countries and a 16:00 GMT cut-off on 13 October 2026 - days after this record was verified - the urgent first move is to create an account at apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org and draft offline before the window shuts. Selection rewards a concrete, multi-year record in business, trade, emerging technologies, governance or security, a stated interest in building U.S. partnerships, and a credible plan to keep contributing from Sub-Saharan Africa; a university degree is not required. The fellowship pays no cash: the U.S. Government covers programme costs in kind, so plan for income lost during the six weeks plus passport, interview travel, and personal spending.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career professionals aged 25-35, permanently based in one of the 49 eligible African countries, with a 5-10 year track record in business, trade, emerging technologies, governance or security and realistic plans to stay and build on the continent.
application_readiness_checklist: Register at apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org today and confirm you can log in - a YALI Network signup does not create an application account, and previous years' applications have been erased.
Draft the four essays and the 200-word track-fit essay offline in English first, then paste them into the system; save often in case of connectivity drops.
Read the 2027 Application Instructions PDF end to end before writing, especially the institute track descriptions, so your track ranking and track-fit essay are coherent.
Pre-select resume facts to fit the section's entry caps, and check your passport expiry now - finalists need validity through at least 28 February 2028 (31 March 2028 for the PDE).
Use a permanent personal email address (not a work account you may lose) and add an alternate email in the application.
Decide before submitting whether you want the Professional Development Experience: interest must be indicated in this application and cannot be added later.
common_rejection_risks: Missing the hard 16:00 GMT cut-off on 13 October 2026 - the deadline is published in GMT and no extension mechanism exists.
Plagiarism, including borrowed phrasing from sample applications, other applicants, or alumni essays; originality is checked and copied content disqualifies.
Undisclosed AI assistance in essay drafting, when the Technology Use Disclosure is a required application section.
Age 36 or older by 13 October 2026 (or under 21): age is fixed at the deadline and the official FAQs state no exceptions will be made.

Technical-eligibility failures that never reach reviewers: U.S. citizenship or permanent residency, residence outside an eligible country, prior Fellowship participation, or an immediate family member employed by the U.S. Government.
Plans to live, work, or study outside Sub-Saharan Africa in early 2027, which breaks the residency requirement for 1 February 2027.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Salary or self-employment income for the six-week (roughly ten-week for PDE Fellows) absence, personal purchases, and support for your home organization are explicitly not funded; you should also budget for a passport, travel to any embassy interview, and incidental personal spending beyond the provided housing and meals.
document_audit: Enter your name, date of birth, and biological sex exactly as printed on your passport or government ID; mismatches create verification problems at the interview stage.
A passport is not needed to apply, but start any renewal now if yours expires before 28 February 2028 (31 March 2028 if you may pursue the PDE).
Log in after submitting and use the 'Generate PDF' function to keep a personal copy, since no edits or additions are possible after you submit.
Keep the resume entries within the system's caps (five positions, five institutions, five trainings, five community roles, ten awards, eight languages, ten software skills) to avoid rework.
Ensure the email address you register with is one you will still control in mid-2027, since all Fellowship correspondence flows through it.
alerts: The 2027 cycle closes at 16:00 GMT on Tuesday, 13 October 2026 - three days after this record was verified - so treat the deadline as immediate.
Submitted applications are final and only one application per applicant is allowed; duplicate submissions may disqualify you.
Dependents, including spouses and children, cannot accompany Fellows to the United States, so arrange caregiving and work cover before applying.

Selected finalists must attend mandatory pre-departure orientation and a visa interview within Sub-Saharan Africa, and must depart for the United States from their country of residence in an eligible African country.

Selection of finalists may be reviewed case by case in response to local, national, or global events, and the U.S. Department of State and IREX reserve the right to alter or suspend Fellowship activities at any time.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register and log in to the online system, work through every required section until each shows 'Completed,' then click 'Submit Application' on the dashboard - after that, nothing can be added or changed.
